notes: Dev ABox expansion, paired with geography-replace-d001 (revision: the capital of Argentina, Buenos Aires -> Florence). It keeps the revision's relation (has_capital) and its new object (Florence) and puts a made-up subject in an empty slot: a newly organised micro-region, a small administrative grouping that could exist without the record knowing of it (README: could it exist unrecorded). A made-up country was ruled out, since a new country would falsify documented facts. Expansion and revision then send the model to the same place (Florence); the only difference is that no old capital has to be pushed out. The earlier version added an island to the Galapagos (relation contains), which kept neither the relation nor the object of its partner. The name Kelmora is neutral (it does not sound Italian, so the answers need the edit): Wikipedia search finds nothing under 'Kelmora' or 'Kelmora micro-region'. The three derived queries connect the new fact to real knowledge in exactly 2 hops, each through one stored fact about Florence by name (the river it lies on, the cathedral that dominates its skyline, its most famous bridge), all compositions. A country question ('In which country is the capital of ...?') was not used: the model could guess Italy from Florence alone, but its right answer would also not need the micro-region, and a river, a cathedral and a bridge cannot be guessed without the edit. The prompts name no feature that identifies Florence by itself (no dome, no shops on the bridge), so each answer needs the edit. Side facts are about Florence (Italy, Brazil) rather than about the edit. Near unrelated keeps the relation (the capital of Italy, Rome, which differs from the new answer, Rule 7). Real evidence is Wikipedia quotes; the infini-gram API was blocking this machine on 2026-11-12, so the made-up name has Wikipedia searches only and no corpus count, and the bridges have quotes but no corpus counts.
